mainTopic: Who owns a wife's extra work, and how שמואל's ruling on a wife's קונם fits with the rule that one cannot consecrate what does not yet exist.
overview: The amud opens with a מחלוקת about what the husband's food (מזונות) and weekly coin (מעה כסף) pay for. רב ושמואל say food pays for her regular work and the coin pays for her extra work (מותר). רב אדא בר אהבה says the reverse, so the husband who feeds her owns the מותר. The גמרא explains that one side pairs common with common and the other pairs fixed with fixed. A ברייתא and a משנה are each brought as challenges, and both are answered by rereading them. Then שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, that a husband cannot consecrate earnings that do not exist yet. This seems to clash with his ruling like רבי יוחנן בן נורי about a wife's קונם on her earnings. The גמרא tries several answers: רב יוסף says vows are different, and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says she vowed on her hands, which already exist. That answer leads to a debate, using the case of a sold field, about whether a הקדש can take effect later when it cannot take effect now. רב פפא's comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב ושמואל: food pays for her work, the coin pays for her extra work
steps.stepSummary: The end of רב ושמואל's view: מזונות were set in exchange for her regular work, and the מעה כסף in exchange for the מותר. So a husband who does not give the מעה כסף has no claim to the מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The חכמים set up] food in exchange for her work, and a silver מעה in exchange for her extra work. Since he is not giving her the silver מעה, the extra work is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes stating the opinion of רב ושמואל from the line just before this section. Each thing the husband gives is matched with something the wife gives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two 'trades.' First, food is paid back by her required work. Second, the small coin (מעה כסף) is paid back by any extra work she does beyond the requirement. In the case being discussed the husband does not give her the coin, so he has not 'paid' for the extra work, and it stays hers.

keyTerms.meaning: Food, the wife's support that the husband must provide
Her handiwork, the fixed amount of work a wife owes her husband
A small silver coin the husband gives his wife weekly for her personal needs
The surplus, whatever work she produces beyond the required amount

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מעשה ידיה with מותר. מעשה ידיה is the basic amount she owes. מותר is only the extra beyond that amount.

phrases.english: [They set up] food in exchange for her work,
and a silver מעה in exchange for the extra work,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּלָא קָא יָהֵיב לַהּ מָעָה כֶּסֶף —
phrases.english: and since he is not giving her a silver מעה,
the extra work is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ושמואל's statement begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מזונות correspond to מעשה ידיה and the מעה כסף corresponds to the מותר. Without the מעה כסף, the מותר belongs to the wife.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: food pays for the extra work, the coin pays for her work
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה reverses the matching: מזונות correspond to the מותר and the מעה כסף to her regular work. Since the husband feeds her, the מותר belongs to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה holds: they set up food in exchange for the extra work, and a silver מעה in exchange for her work. Since he gives her food, the extra work is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion is stated. It uses the same pieces as רב ושמואל but swaps which payment matches which kind of work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here food buys the extra work. Since the husband is feeding her, he has paid for the מותר, so it is his. The result is the opposite of רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) set up, made it an enactment
Aramaic for food or support

steps.whyThisMatters: Who owns the מותר decides whether the husband has rights over it. This is the practical question the whole מחלוקת is about.

phrases.english: רב אדא בר אהבה holds:
they set up food in exchange for the extra work,
and a silver מעה in exchange for her work,
and since he gives her food,
the extra work is his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the opposing view to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מזונות correspond to the מותר and the מעה כסף corresponds to מעשה ידיה. Since he feeds her, the מותר is the husband's.

steps.title: What is the reason behind the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea each side's matching is built on.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next step by asking for the reasoning behind the two opposite matchings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that each payment matches some kind of work. The question is why each side pairs them the way it does.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (a request for the underlying reason)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind steps 1 and 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic that leads each side to its pairing.

steps.title: Common matched with common, or fixed matched with fixed
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל pair the two things that happen regularly: food and her required work. רב אדא בר אהבה pairs the two things with a set amount: the מעה כסף and her fixed work quota.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds: something common [is matched] with something common. The other master holds: something fixed [is matched] with something fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving each side a simple pairing rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב ושמואל, food is something she always needs and her work is something she always does, so the two everyday things go together. That leaves the coin paired with the extra work. For רב אדא בר אהבה, the coin is a set amount and her work quota is a set amount, so the two measured things go together. That leaves food paired with the extra work.

keyTerms.meaning: One master holds (introduces one side of a מחלוקת)
Something common, that happens all the time
Something fixed, with a set amount

steps.whatToRemember: רב ושמואל pair what is common: food goes with her work. רב אדא בר אהבה pairs what is fixed: the coin goes with her work quota.

phrases.english: One master holds:
something common [is matched] with something common.
And the other master holds:
phrases.notes: This second 'master' is רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: something fixed [is matched] with something fixed.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר מִידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ מִמִּידֵּי דִּשְׁכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ושמואל pair common with common (food with work). רב אדא בר אהבה pairs fixed with fixed (מעה כסף with the work quota).

steps.title: A ברייתא says food is for her work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה from a ברייתא that pairs מזונות with מעשה ידיה, exactly like רב ושמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: They set up food in exchange for her work!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה said food is for the extra work. The ברייתא plainly says food is for her work, which matches רב ושמואל.

phrases.english: They challenged [from a ברייתא]:
They set up food in exchange for her work!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אדא בר אהבה's view from step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא pairs מזונות with מעשה ידיה, not with the מותר.

steps.title: Read it as 'the extra of her work'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is reread to mean that food is in exchange for the מותר of her work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: in exchange for the extra of her work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב אדא בר אהבה by saying the ברייתא should be read as talking about the extra work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one word added, 'מותר', the ברייתא now matches רב אדא בר אהבה. The challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the source this way instead)

phrases.english: Say: in exchange for the extra of her work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא pairs food with her regular work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means food is for the מותר of her work.

steps.title: A משנה ties the coin to her work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a משנה: if he does not give her the מעה כסף, her work is hers. This suggests the coin pays for her regular work, which goes against רב ושמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If he does not give her a silver מעה for her needs, her work is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the challenge goes the other way, against רב ושמואל, from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If skipping the coin means he loses her work, then the coin must be what pays for her work. That is רב אדא בר אהבה's pairing, not רב ושמואל's.

keyTerms.meaning: For her needs

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֵינוֹ נוֹתֵן לָהּ מָעָה כֶּסֶף לִצְרָכֶיהָ —
phrases.english: If he does not give her a silver מעה for her needs,
her work is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב אדא בר אהבה to challenging רב ושמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה links the מעה כסף with מעשה ידיה, not with the מותר.

steps.title: Read it as 'the extra of her work is hers'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is reread so that only the מותר goes to her when he skips the coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: the extra of her work is hers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ושמואל the same way as before, by reading 'מותר' into the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With that reading, the coin is tied to the extra work, just as רב ושמואל said.

phrases.english: Say: the extra of her work is hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives her all her work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה gives her only the מותר.

steps.title: The משנה's next line is about her required work
steps.stepSummary: The rereading is attacked. The same משנה goes on to give a fixed amount she must produce for him, five סלעים of warp thread in יהודה. That shows the משנה is talking about her required work, not the extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on this very case it teaches: What does she make for him? The weight of five סלעים of warp thread in יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 8 using the continuation of the same משנה. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a fixed quota she owes. That shows the משנה is discussing her basic required work. So reading 'מותר' into the earlier line looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: But on this very case it teaches (the same source says more)
סלעים, a unit of weight (and coin)
Warp, the lengthwise threads in weaving

steps.confusionAlert: Here the five סלעים are a weight of thread she must spin, not money.

phrases.english: But on this very case it teaches:
What does she make for him?
The weight of five סלעים of warp thread in יהודה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rereading offered in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rereading of the משנה in step 8 (defending רב ושמואל)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's continuation sets a fixed quota, so it is about her required work and not the מותר.

steps.title: The fixed amount tells us where the extra begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה gives the five סלעים amount only so we know how much her required work is, and anything beyond it is the מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: how much is her required work, so we can know how much her extra is? The weight of five סלעים of warp thread in יהודה, which equals ten סלעים in the גליל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9. The fixed amount is not proof that the משנה is about her regular work. It is there to show where the extra starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9 the fixed amount seemed to prove the משנה was talking about her required work. Now the גמרא says the amount sets the line: up to five סלעים is required work, and anything past it is the מותר. So the reading from step 8 still works, and it fits רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Used to reread a text.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
How much is her required work,
so that one can know how much her extra is?
The weight of five סלעים of warp thread in יהודה,
which is ten סלעים in the גליל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and supports the rereading from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the purpose of a clause in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fixed amount shows that the משנה is talking about her required work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fixed amount only marks where required work ends, so we can identify the מותר.

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר about consecrating a wife's earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling from שמואל on the earlier מחלוקת about a husband who consecrates his wife's earnings. This ruling sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר holds that the husband's consecration does not take hold on her earnings, because those earnings do not exist yet. שמואל agrees with him. In the next step the גמרא checks whether this fits with another ruling of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The final ruling follows this opinion

phrases.english: שמואל said:
The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה's case of a husband consecrating his wife's earnings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the final ruling on the משנה's מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן הסנדלר. A husband's consecration does not take hold on earnings that do not exist yet.

steps.title: שמואל seems to contradict himself about the קונם case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about a wife's קונם on her earnings, where שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן בן נורי. That view seems to let a vow take hold on earnings that do not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did שמואל really say that? We learned in a משנה: if a woman says, 'What I make for your mouth is קונם,' the husband does not need to cancel the vow. רבי עקיבא says: he should cancel it, in case she produces more than she owes him. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: he should cancel it, in case he divorces her and she becomes forbidden to remarry him. And שמואל said: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling from step 11. It shows that in a different case, שמואל ruled in a way that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי worries that after a divorce the vow will take hold on her future earnings, so he treats a vow as able to take hold on things that do not exist yet. When שמואל rules like him, he seems to disagree with רבי יוחנן הסנדלר, whom he just followed.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say that? This opens a contradiction.
A vow that makes something forbidden like a קרבן
To cancel a vow. A husband can cancel some of his wife's vows.
She produces extra

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people named רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר is from step 11, and רבי יוחנן בן נורי is from this משנה. The challenge works because שמואל seems to follow both, and they seem to disagree.

phrases.english: But did שמואל really say this?
But we learned in a משנה:
'What I make for your mouth is קונם' —
he does not need to cancel the vow.
רבי עקיבא says: he should cancel it,
in case she produces extra for him
beyond what is due to him.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אָמַר: יָפֵר,
phrases.english: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: he should cancel it,
in case he divorces her
and she will be forbidden to come back to him.
phrases.notes: If he remarried her, he would benefit from earnings she had forbidden to him.

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 11 with another ruling of his own.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן בן נורי lets a vow take hold on future earnings that do not exist yet. When שמואל follows him, he seems to contradict his ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.

steps.title: שמואל agreed only about the extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל followed רבי יוחנן בן נורי only regarding the העדפה, the extra work.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, he meant only regarding the extra.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 12. It limits שמואל's agreement with רבי יוחנן בן נורי to the extra work only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, the two rulings are no longer about the same thing. The ruling like רבי יוחנן בן נורי covers only the העדפה. It does not show that שמואל holds a vow takes hold on all her future earnings, so his ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר can stand.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said. This limits what a ruling covers.
The extra, meaning work beyond what she owes her husband

phrases.english: When שמואל said
the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי,
it was regarding the extra.
phrases.notes: This is the same 'extra' רבי עקיבא spoke about: what she produces beyond what she owes him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, לְהַעְדָּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל followed רבי יוחנן בן נורי for all her future earnings, which would clash with רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל followed רבי יוחנן בן נורי only regarding the העדפה.

steps.title: Why did שמואל not say it more clearly?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 13. If שמואל meant to agree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי only about the העדפה, he should have said so outright, or used a clearer phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי regarding the extra work! Or he could say: The הלכה does not follow the תנא קמא! Or: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. If שמואל only meant the extra work, his words should have said that clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל made a general statement that the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The גמרא lists three clearer ways he could have said that he meant only the העדפה. Since he did not use any of them, the limited reading looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him say (he should have said it this way)
Or else / alternatively
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְהַעְדָּפָה!
phrases.english: Then let him say: The halakha follows Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri regarding the surplus!
phrases.notes: The surplus is the extra work she does beyond what she owes her husband, from step 13.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא!
phrases.english: Or alternatively: The halakha does not follow the first tanna!
Or alternatively: The halakha follows Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי לְהַעְדָּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that שמואל followed רבי יוחנן בן נורי only regarding the העדפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his ruling were that narrow, he would have worded it narrowly. There were three clearer ways to say it, and he used none of them.

steps.title: רב יוסף: vows are different
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new answer. קונמות have special power and can take hold even on things not yet in the world. So שמואל's ruling about vows does not contradict his ruling about הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: You are bringing a proof from vows? Vows are different. Since a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself, a person can also consecrate something that has not yet come into the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the step 13 answer and brings a new way to solve the contradiction in שמואל's rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says קונמות have unusual strength. A person can forbid to himself produce he does not even own. Because of this, a vow can also take hold on something that does not exist yet. That is an exception for vows only, so שמואל can still hold like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר for regular הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows that forbid something, using the word קונם
It is different
Another person's produce
Something that does not exist yet

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא here means the answer of step 13 is being dropped. רב יוסף is answering the question from step 12 in a new way.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Are you speaking about konamot?
phrases.notes: He means: you're trying to prove something about הקדש from a case of vows.

phrases.english: Konamot are different,

phrases.aramaic: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁאָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו,
phrases.english: since a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְדִּישׁ דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: a person can consecrate something that has not come into the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: קֻוֽנָּמוֹת קָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new answer to the step 12 contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (vows versus regular הקדש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's ruling on vows seemed to show that anything can take hold on things not yet in the world
steps.terutzMaskana: Vows have special power, so ruling like רבי יוחנן בן נורי on vows does not contradict ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר on הקדש

steps.title: אביי: a vow cannot forbid to someone else
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's comparison. You can forbid your friend's produce to yourself only because one side of the vow belongs to you. A wife forbidding not-yet-existing earnings to her husband has neither side in her hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: It makes sense that a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself, because a person can forbid his own produce to his friend. But should he be able to forbid something not yet in the world to his friend? A person cannot forbid one friend's produce to another friend!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's answer and shows that the special power of vows does not stretch far enough for our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every vow that works, something is in the person's control: either his own body or his own produce. The wife's earnings do not exist yet and the vow is aimed at her husband. That is like forbidding someone else's produce to a third person, which never works.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that... (this part is fine)
Because / since
Should he be able to forbid?

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו —
phrases.english: Granted, a person can forbid his friend's produce to himself —

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹתָיו עַל חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: because a person can forbid his own produce to his friend.

phrases.aramaic: יֶאֱסֹר דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לְעוֹלָם עַל חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: Should he forbid something that has not come into the world to his friend,
phrases.notes: This is a question: how can the wife forbid earnings that don't exist yet to her husband?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן אֵין אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עַל חֲבֵירוֹ?
phrases.english: when a person cannot forbid his friend's produce to another friend?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא אָדָם אוֹסֵר פֵּירוֹת חֲבֵירוֹ עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the power of vows explains why a vow takes hold on things not yet in the world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forbidding a friend's produce to yourself works only because one side, your own body, is yours. When the item does not exist and the vow is aimed at another person, nothing is in your control. That is like forbidding someone's produce to a third person, which does not work.

steps.title: She vowed on her hands, which already exist
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the משנה is talking about a woman who said 'My hands are consecrated to the One who made them.' Her hands already exist, so the vow can take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב הונא the son of רב יהושע said: The case is where she says, 'May my hands be consecrated to the One who made them.' Hands do exist in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב יוסף's answer and gives a new explanation that removes the contradiction in שמואל's rulings. The next steps test this explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow is not on her future earnings but on her hands, which exist right now. So ruling like רבי יוחנן בן נורי here does not mean something can take hold on what is not yet in the world. שמואל can still follow רבי יוחנן הסנדלר.

keyTerms.meaning: May my hands be consecrated to the One who made them
They exist in the world

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's ruling like רבי יוחנן בן נורי on a wife's vow works because she vowed on her hands, which already exist. So it does not clash with his ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר that a person cannot consecrate what does not yet exist.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the rule that a person cannot consecrate something not yet in the world. A vow can still work if it is placed on an existing source, like the hands.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is where she says, 'May my hands be consecrated to their Maker,'
phrases.notes: 'Their Maker' means ה׳, who made her hands.

phrases.english: for the hands exist in the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected answer with a new case definition that answers the question from step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (the vow is on existing hands, not on future earnings)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wife's vow seemed to be on earnings that do not exist yet
steps.terutzMaskana: She vowed on her hands, which exist, so there is no contradiction with ruling like רבי יוחנן הסנדלר

steps.title: Her hands are tied to her husband, so how can she consecrate them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: even if she says 'my hands are consecrated,' her husband has a claim on her work, so the הקדש should not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when she says this, does it really become consecrated? She is obligated to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 17. It asks how her hands can become הקדש when her husband has rights to what they produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said the vow works because her hands already exist. The problem is not existence but ownership. Her work is שעבוד to her husband, and you cannot consecrate something another person has rights to.

keyTerms.meaning: Obligated or bound. Here it means her work is owed to her husband.
Becomes consecrated (הקדש).
She says.

phrases.english: But when she says this
phrases.notes: 'This' means 'My hands are consecrated to the One who made them' from step 17.

phrases.english: does it become consecrated?
She is obligated to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's claim that consecrating her hands takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her hands' output is owed to her husband, so she lacks the power to make them הקדש.

steps.title: She meant it to take effect once she is divorced
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that she said the הקדש would start when she gets divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where she said: when I get divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 18. She tied the הקדש to a future time when her husband no longer has any claim on her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After divorce, her husband's rights are gone, so nothing blocks the הקדש. This answer creates a new question, though: can something become הקדש later if it cannot become הקדש now?

keyTerms.meaning: When she gets divorced.

phrases.english: Where she said: when I get divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case by adding a time condition.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was meant to take effect immediately, while she is still married.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow is set to take effect after divorce, when the husband's rights are gone.

steps.title: Can something become הקדש later if it cannot become הקדש now?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea of a delayed הקדש. Something that cannot be consecrated now should not be able to become consecrated in the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there anything that cannot be consecrated now and yet becomes consecrated later?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 19. It doubts that a הקדש can kick in later when it has no power to take effect now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right now she cannot consecrate her hands because her husband has a claim on them. The גמרא assumes that if the act cannot work now, saying it now should not make it work later.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at present.
Later, in the future.
Is consecrated.

phrases.english: But is there anything
that now is not consecrated
and later becomes consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא מִידֵּי דְּאִילּוּ הַשְׁתָּא לָא קַדִּישׁ וּלְקַמֵּיהּ קַדִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that she can consecrate her hands to take effect after divorce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הקדש that cannot take effect now should not be able to take effect later.

steps.title: רבי אלעאי: a field consecrated for after it is bought back
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעאי says a delayed הקדש can work. He compares it to a man who sells a field and says it should become הקדש when he buys it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעאי said: Why not? If a person says to his friend, 'This field that I am selling to you, when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated,' doesn't it become consecrated?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעאי answers step 20 with an example. A seller can arrange for the field to become הקדש later, after he buys it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the buyer owns the field, the seller cannot consecrate it. Still, his words take effect once he buys it back. So something can become הקדש later even though it cannot become הקדש in between.

keyTerms.meaning: Why not?
When I buy it back.
Let it be consecrated.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elai said: Why not?
If one says to his friend
"This field that I am selling to you,
when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated,"
doesn't it become consecrated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20 with a comparison case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a parallel case to show a delayed הקדש works.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing can become הקדש later if it cannot become הקדש now.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seller can make a field become הקדש once he buys it back, so a delayed הקדש can work.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the field case is different
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the comparison. The seller still owned the field when he spoke, but the wife has no power to divorce herself. A better comparison is a field that was already sold, and that one does not become הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה objects: Are they comparable? There, it is in his power to consecrate it. Here, it is not in her power to divorce herself. This is comparable only to one who says to his friend, 'This field that I already sold to you, when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated,' and there it does not become consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on רבי אלעאי's proof. He says the wife's case is like a field that was already sold, and that delayed הקדש fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the seller spoke, the field was still his, so he had full power over it. The wife cannot end her marriage by herself, so right now she has no control over her hands' work. That matches a field already sold, where the seller has no control, and the הקדש fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it.
Are they comparable?
In his power.
That I already sold.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objects to it:
Are they comparable?
There, it is in his power to consecrate it.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא, אֵין בְּיָדָהּ לְגָרֵשׁ אֶת עַצְמָהּ.
phrases.english: Here, it is not in her power to divorce herself.
This is comparable only
to one who says to his friend
"This field that I sold to you,
when I buy it back from you, let it be consecrated,"
where it is not consecrated.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the difference between שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹכֵר ('that I am selling,' step 21) and שֶׁמָּכַרְתִּי ('that I already sold'). That small difference in wording is the whole argument.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעאי's comparison from step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the field case only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The seller had power over the field when he spoke. The wife has no power to end her husband's rights, so her case matches a field already sold, where the הקדש fails.

steps.title: רב פפא: the already-sold field is different too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects רבי ירמיה's comparison. In the sold field, the buyer owns both the field and its produce, but the wife still owns her own body. He begins offering a better comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objects: Are they comparable? There, the field itself and its produce are in the buyer's hands. Here, her body is in her own hands. This is comparable only to one who says to his friend...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on רבי ירמיה. He starts to give a more accurate comparison, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sold field, the seller has nothing left at all. The wife still owns her hands, and her husband only has rights to what they produce. So her case is stronger than the sold field, and רבי ירמיה's comparison does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: The thing itself (here, the land or her body).
Produce or profits that come from something.
Buyer.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: מִי דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: Rav Pappa objects to it: Are they comparable?
There, the body and the produce
are in the hand of the buyer.
Here, her body is in her hand.
phrases.notes: She owns her hands themselves. Her husband only has rights to what they produce.

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: This is comparable only to one who says to his friend

steps.whyThisMatters: The line between owning the thing itself (גוף) and only having rights to its produce (פירות) decides whether a delayed הקדש can work.
steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא מִי דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי ירמיה's counter-comparison from step 22 and begins a new one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי ירמיה's comparison to the already-sold field.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the sold field, the buyer holds both the land and its produce. The wife still owns her body and loses only its earnings, so the cases are not the same.
